note: The BirdNET asset the release build fetches, pinned by digest.
The digest lives HERE, in the repository, and not in the remote manifest. Reading the
expected hash from the same server that serves the file verifies nothing: a mirror that
swapped the model would swap its manifest in the same breath. Pinned here, a changed file
fails the build and a deliberate upgrade is a commit somebody can read.
BirdNET V3.0 publishes on Zenodo, which this project's network cannot reach (VERIFICATION
§61). These bytes come from a third-party mirror and matched the digests that mirror
publishes; they have not been checked against Zenodo's own. Said plainly because it is the
kind of thing that is easy to forget once it works.
fp32 rather than fp16: ONNX Runtime upconverts fp16 on CPU, so it is slower and saves no
memory — the same conclusion §21 reached for the vision model.
